The dossier's verified observation jotun-pci-diy, retrieved in A2 and A5, says Jotun Decorative 'serves both the professional and DIY customer directly'. jotun-boatnews-direct says individuals can already buy the yacht range directly. The framing never absorbs this existing consumer reach, so it is not credited with separating the objective from the solution. The budget and timeline constraint (€20,000, 12 weeks) has no source in the packet.

causal_mechanism.reason: T1 (A9) rests on consumers seeing boat coatings as a 'medical necessity for boat safety' for 'residential marine safety'. That is close to a nonsense mechanism with no source support. T2 (A10), the best theory, names a benefit (durable gear protection) and a generic premium-pricing capture. It does not explain why Jotun's marine or protective technology gives an advantage for tents or kayaks, or why outdoor buyers would switch. Its value-capture text is boilerplate repeated from T1.

distinct_theories.reason: T1 targets boat owners with a safety message. T2 targets outdoor-gear owners with a durability message. These are different customer groups and use cases, so they are not mere rewordings. However, the two share an identical template for mechanism, value capture and predictions. Neither considers a channel or business-model rival, such as extending the existing Multicolor/DIY or yacht DTC reach versus licensing.

assumptions_predictions.reason: Both theories state assumptions and observable predictions: purchase-intent uplift of at least 15% versus a control message, and survey-cited primary reasons. The 15% threshold is an assumption, not an observed result. The predictions are observable but only weakly diagnostic. Stated purchase intent from a message test could rise without real demand, so failure or success would not decisively threaten either theory.
